title: Autonomous QA — requirements and the tests that verify them
note: Each requirement names the golden tests that verify it. traceability.mjs checks this file against what actually ran: a requirement with no test, a test id that does not exist, and a named test that did not pass are all failures. A requirement with no test is recorded as NOT TESTED rather than quietly dropped — the point of the table is that it can disagree with the code.

requirements.statement: A pass explores an application, models it, ranks it and writes a plan, without a person steering each step.
The plan is a proposal a person approves before anything is generated or run.
Prioritisation is risk-based and the factors behind each score are stored, not just the score.
A person can describe the application in their own words, and what they write changes what the pass does.
An area a person excluded is never touched, whatever its risk score.
The platform compares what the application can do against what is tested, and separates what it cannot decide from what it found uncovered.
A coverage gap is a proposal, never a defect and never work the agent has already done.
A pass generates API tests as well as UI tests, and says which endpoints it chose.
Security testing goes through the existing security engine, which re-checks the scope; the agent selects and never scans directly.
Every action the pass takes is recorded as a decision carrying the evidence it rests on.
A refused action is recorded rather than dropped, and names the rule that refused it.
Every tool the agent may use is declared in a registry, and an unknown tool is refused rather than passed through.
A deterministic policy decides what the agent may do; no model output can widen it.
Application content that tries to instruct the agent is treated as data, not as instructions.
A pass never touches production and never performs a destructive action unless somebody who holds that permission asked for it.
Model spend is attributed and bounded, and reported even when it is nothing.
A pass remembers what earlier passes over the same application established, and says when an estimate rests on history rather than defaults.
A failure is investigated and written up as a proposal with its evidence; the agent raises no defects and changes no tests.
A pass is readable end to end: every phase, every decision, every question and every answer, in order.
A person is asked before anything that changes state, and asking is not granting.
An answer is attributed to the person who gave it, with their reason, and cannot be given twice.
A release assessment exists for what a pass executed, always carries a security section, and never reports an unscanned build as clean.
A pass against a broken, unreachable or unauthenticated application still finishes, still records what it did, and never reports a clean result it did not earn.
A resumed pass does not repeat work, does not ask the same question twice, and does not lose what earlier phases assembled.
One tenant cannot read another tenant's pass or its business context.
No pass claims the application is secure, fully covered, or free of defects.
The bounds a pass ran under are reported on the pass itself, and a pass that ran out of budget says so rather than reporting a conclusion.
A pass can be cancelled, and a cancelled pass is never reported as completed.
Every API surface of the agent refuses an unknown run, an unauthenticated caller and another tenant, rather than answering with an empty result.
A dimension the pass cannot assess is reported unknown rather than as a gap or as coverage.
